children: Malaysian palm oil futures opened lower on Wednesday after a two-session rally, weighed down by weaker rival edible oils, though stronger crude oil prices lent some support.
The benchmark palm oil contract (FCPOc3) for November delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange slid 33 ringgit, or 0.66%, to 4,940 ringgit ($1,222.47) a metric ton in early trade.

Oil prices rose nearly 1% in early trade, extending the previous session's surge, as concerns over supply disruption intensified after the U.S. and Iran exchanged strikes overnight, dimming hopes for a quick easing of tensions in the Middle East. O/R
Stronger crude oil futures make palm a more attractive option for biodiesel feedstock.
Dalian's most-active soyoil contract (DBYcv1) fell 0.02%, while its palm oil contract
shed 0.93%. Soyoil prices on the Chicago Board of Trade (BOcv1) were down 0.59%.
Palm oil tracks the price movements of rival edible oils, as it competes for a share of the global vegetable oils market.
, palm's currency of trade, weakened 0.14% against the dollar, making the commodity slightly cheaper for buyers holding foreign currencies.

European Union soybean imports for the 2026/27 season, which began in July, reached 1.87 million tons by August 30, down 25% from a year earlier, while palm oil imports fell 21% to 0.41 million tons, European Commission data showed on Tuesday.
Indonesia exported 2.23 million tons of palm oil in July, up 15.44% on a yearly basis, but exports in the first seven months of this year declined annually, statistics bureau data showed.
Cargo surveyors estimated that exports of Malaysian palm oil products in August fell between 6.5% and 14.9% from a month earlier.
Palm oil may rise into a range of 5,032 ringgit to 5,083 ringgit per ton, as it has almost recovered from a drop to the August 28 low of 4,799 ringgit, Reuters technical analyst Wang Tao said. TECH/C

* Stocks slumped at the start of the Asian trading session on Wednesday as a bond market-induced panic on global markets spilled over into the region, after renewed attacks by the U.S. on Iran pushed oil prices higher. MKTS/GLOB
